newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 6.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:

* Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan said inflation risks remain and that he is ready to act "pre-emptively" to raise interest rates, but he conceded that stock market prices may not be overvalued.
* Surveyed economists say the U.S. economy's growth rate could be increased by one-half percentage point annually if the right policies are pursued.
* Wal-Mart's Canadian subsidiary removed Cuban-made pajamas from its stores, citing concerns that it may be in violation of U.S. trade laws against Cuba.

* B.A.T Industries said its costs from tobacco liability cases last year surged more than 65 percent in the U.S. to $100 million and reiterated that it is willing to consider an industrywide settlement of U.S. litigation.

* Toys R Us said during the opening day of its trial before an administrative law judge that it warned toy makers it might not carry certain toys if the toys were offered to warehouse clubs that sell at a discount.
* A Pennsylvania court threw out an earlier approval for CIGNA's proposed restructuring of its property-casualty business into profitable and ongoing segments and unprofitable, discontinued units.

* A presidential panel ended five days of hearings on the dispute between AMR's American Airlines and its pilots and will likely make a final effort to reach a settlement before making its recommendation.
* The dollar slipped against the yen amid concerns over U.S.-Japan trade figures. The Mexican peso fell to a record low of 8.01 pesos per dollar.
* Chrysler launched a dealer-incentive to boost sales, and Ford is expected to respond.

* Indexing was not as profitable last year for international mutual fund investors. The average return of 317 international mutual funds posted a rise nearly double the return of a benchmark Morgan Stanley index of 20 overseas markets.
* A Moody's report says some U.S. securities firms will have to make acquisitions or merge if they are to become major global players.

* A unit of Florida Power & Light is suing Donovan Leisure Newton & Irvine, accusing the law firm of helping to defraud an investor in a South Carolina power plant project that Florida Power's unit later bought.
* Donna Karan ended its DKNY licensing pact with Designer Holdings, sending Karan's shares falling 5.3 percent to their lowest level since the company went public last summer.

* Small investors long have complained that they can be hurt when companies hold conference calls with analysts and big investors, because the calls give the pros yet another chance to trade first on the news.
Now a study being prepared for publication by three University of Michigan researchers suggests that the small investors may have a point. -- Heard on the Street.

* Treasury securities rebounded from the recent weakness to score their first gains in eight trading sessions, as investors shifted their attention from pronouncements by Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan to tomorrow's release of employment data for February. -- Credit Markets.
